name: Circadian Compression Therapy
description: Modifies the sleep cycle using genes from species that achieve rest through unihemispheric sleep — dolphins and migratory birds that sleep with half their brain at a time. The modification doesn't eliminate sleep but compresses it: the user achieves full cognitive and physical recovery in 2–3 hours instead of 7–8, and the sleep is lighter, with easier arousal. Some installations allow a 'dolphin mode' where one brain hemisphere sleeps while the other remains conscious — the user appears awake and functional but is resting half their brain. Productivity gains are enormous: 4–6 extra hours of functional time per day. The modification is standard among Tier 5 executives, ubiquitous in demanding corporate roles, and increasingly common among Tier 3 professionals who can't afford to sleep while their modified colleagues work. It is, in effect, mandatory in any competitive field where it's available.
source_organism: Tursiops truncatus (bottlenose dolphin), Limosa lapponica (bar-tailed godwit, migratory endurance genes)
tier_availability: Tier 4+ (Zheng-Dao employees receive it as a benefit at Tier 3)
legality: Licensed (labor law implications regarding expected working hours)
procedure: Neural retroviral treatment targeting sleep regulation centers, 8 sessions over 4 months
expression_time: 3–6 months for full sleep compression; dolphin mode 6–12 months
reversibility: Partially reversible; sleep patterns never fully normalize
side_effects: Dreams become rare and when they occur, they are vivid and disturbing
Microsleep episodes during extreme fatigue bypass the modification
Emotional regulation suffers — the deep sleep stages that process emotion are compressed
Long-term users report feeling 'hollow' — present but not fully rested despite physical metrics showing adequate recovery
Social isolation — when you don't sleep, you lose the shared vulnerability that sleep represents
social_perception: The modification that best represents Meridian 88's relationship with human limits. Celebrated as productivity. Criticized as self-exploitation. Required in practice if not in policy. The Sleepless work more, earn more, and burn out in ways that don't show on medical scans.
story_hooks: A Sleepless executive's dolphin-mode hemisphere begins making decisions the conscious hemisphere disagrees with — the sleeping brain is dreaming strategies that the waking brain can't follow
A labor movement in the Shelf demands that sleep-modification requirements be classified as wage theft — if you're required to sleep less to keep your job, the extra hours are unpaid labor
